soundness_flags.label: def:target; lem:identification-fwl; thm:sharp-joint-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: The target uses a generic unit i but no event-date replication/exchangeability condition makes the treated sample average target that conditional mean; ass:within-site-replication applies only to Q, not B(1).

soundness_flags.label: def:fwl-regression and lem:identification-fwl
soundness_flags.one_line: The FWL construction does not specify polynomial regressors or their values on event rows, exact row weights, or fold stacking, so theta_FWL is not a defined regression coefficient whose exact equality to hat_tau can be assessed.

soundness_flags.label: prop:volatility-drag
soundness_flags.one_line: “Mean-only donor matching” is not a defined observation map or estimator class, and the displayed one-law product inequality does not itself establish a two-law nonidentification result for a mean-only procedure.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:event-transport; identification and all downstream targets
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Cross-date counterfactual transport is maintained rather than testable at the treated event date.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Identification, estimation, and inference are conditional on ass:event-transport.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:local-two-sided-modulus; thm:sharp-joint-frontier and thm:honest-length-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The nonflat covariance-standardized local modulus, which supplies the donor lower channel, is assumed rather than derived from the Holder ball.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The matched donor-channel frontier is conditional on ass:local-two-sided-modulus; this derived-versus-assumed dependency caps the proposal at field tier.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies financial event-study causal effects under factor-model misspecification, discusses buy-and-hold abnormal returns and variance considerations, and analyzes synthetic-control and factor-model estimators.
The paper gives repeated-measurement Holder regression rates of order n^{-1}+(nm)^{-2s/(2s+d)} up to logarithmic factors and a sparse-to-dense phase transition.
The article studies pointwise random-design regression, local-polynomial/Lepski adaptation, local design mass, and Holder-type local smoothness.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics 49(1) (1997)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article analyzes local-polynomial regression, including multivariate local-linear minimax properties and boundary/design adaptation.
The paper analyzes nonparametric regression with covariates estimated in a preliminary step and derives stochastic expansions for their effect.
The paper treats replicated classical measurement error and deconvolution for density and errors-in-variables regression, including ordinary- and supersmooth cases.
The paper estimates the minimizer and minimum of a smooth strongly convex regression function; its two-stage construction evaluates a local-polynomial estimator at a first-stage estimated minimizer.

The paper develops synthetic-control prediction intervals with weight-estimation and post-treatment uncertainty; Appendix A extends the construction to conditional beta-mixing data using large- and small-block controls.
The article establishes optimal sup-norm series rates and functional asymptotic normality under weak dependence using random-matrix concentration.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear functionals over convex regression classes under normal errors with known variance.
The paper studies synthetic-control asymptotics when both pretreatment periods and controls grow, under a linear factor model.
The article introduces proximal identification and inference for synthetic controls using controls excluded from SC construction as proxies for latent confounders.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Either define tau as the conditional finite-cohort average n_s^{-1} sum_i E[B_si(1)-B_si(0)|z_0,E_0], or add conditional identical-distribution/exchangeability assumptions for both B_si(1) and B_si(0).

Write the stacked FWL design algebraically: specify event-row polynomial values, cohort-specific event interactions, weights, donor-fold assignment, and the precise weighted least-squares criterion, then state equality with the same foldwise intercepts used by hat_tau.

Replace the volatility-drag conclusion by a formal two-law theorem: define the mean-only sigma-field or estimator class and construct nondegenerate P0,P1 sharing that information but with distinct tau.
Correct YanYao2023 metadata to the primary arXiv title and listed authors before using it as a checklist citation.
